correctness.rationale: For season map F_{K,h}(x)=mu*K*x/[K+(mu−1)*x]−h on x>0, with mu>1, two H and four L capacities in a 6-cycle, 0<L<H and uniform subtraction h, each F is an increasing fractional-linear map with matrix B_K and det mu*K²>0. Its six-season composition has order-independent determinant Δ=mu^6 H^4 L^8, with collision/disappearance of positive periodic states by tangency at first positive T_d(h)=2sqrt(Δ). Positive states exist for small h; increasing h lowers the period map, and feasible fixed points cannot approach infinity or the zero boundary at a positive h. Every 6-cycle contains two consecutive low seasons, so h cannot reach h0=L(mu+1−sqrt(mu))/(mu−1); indeed F_L,h0(sup F_L,h0)=−L/(mu−1)<0. On 0<h<h0, t=L(mu+1)−h(mu−1)>sqrt(mu)*L. Explicit expansion of the two-high-season trace gives T2−T1=h² mu(H−L)²(mu−1)²(t²−mu L²)>0 and T3−T2=h² mu² L²(H−L)²(mu−1)²>0. All first positive roots of T_d−2sqrtΔ lie in (0,h0), thus their strictly ordered functions have strictly ordered first roots h1<h2<h3. Independently recomputed BOTH full symbolic trace differences with SymPy, determinant, and rational brackets at (mu,L,H)=(4,1,4); no finite numerical sample is substituted for the all-parameter proof.
